name: manual_01a9f1
claim: A CodeRabbit review comment's stated line number is a snapshot against the commit it reviewed, not a durable pointer -- if the target file has grown or been edited since (new commits, other agents' concurrent pushes), re-locate the finding by its quoted content or code snippet before assuming the line reference is still valid. A stale line reference pointing at unrelated content is a signal the finding may already be resolved or moved, not a signal to force a fix at the wrong location.

decisions.notes: On PT PR #258, a 'bootstrap banned-attribution-patterns before running the scan' nitpick cited AGENT_LEARNINGS.jsonl lines 223-226, but by the time it was addressed the file had grown from ~180 to 237+ lines from concurrent commits, and those line numbers pointed at entirely unrelated, much more recent content. Correctly treated as stale-and-skip rather than editing the wrong lines to satisfy the letter of the comment.
